title: A pipeline for STED super-resolution imaging and Imaris analysis of nanoscale synapse organization in mouse cortical brain slices
protocol: Select 485 nm excitation laser line for GFP IUE cell fill.
Select 561 nm excitation laser line for Abberior STAR Orange for GluR1.
Select 640 nm excitation laser line for Abberior STAR Red for LAMP1.
Select 775 nm STED depletion laser line for Abberior STAR Orange and Abberior STAR Red.
Localize ROIs to L1 apical dendritic tufts from L2/3 pyramidal cells in the mPFC.
Maintain strict selection criteria when imaging the morphology and density of dendritic spines in the cerebral cortex.
Select regions that are away from the dendritic tuft end or the branching region.
Find a dendritic shaft segment at least 30 μm long, parallel to the horizontal plane.
Ensure that much of the segment is located within a few Z-steps.
Choose dendritic segments isolated from other cells.
Set the Z stack according to the cell fill channel.
Add a few sections of space above and below the dendrite.
Acquire images from dendritic shafts and synaptic markers localized to apical dendritic tufts in L1 as stacks of approximately 20–60 optical sections.
Maintain an X/Y resolution of 40 px/μm.
Double the confocal excitation power value for STED excitation.
Set the STED depletion laser power setting so that it does not detract from signal intensity compared to the confocal test and does not degrade image quality.
Stain transfected GFP-positive cells and processes with an anti-GFP primary antibody at a 1:500 dilution.
Apply Abberior STAR Orange secondary antibody at a 1:300 dilution for the cell fill signal compatible with STED imaging.
Use Abberior STAR Red secondary antibody at a 1:1000 dilution when necessary.
Consider the power to counts ratio for resolving small structures such as necks without bleaching the sample during STED imaging.
Reduce optical aberrations by combining STED with hollow Bessel beams or adaptive optics techniques.
